code.commit_subject: variants FINDINGS 3: unseen-bench bug + fix, baselines (seed 175/200 vs supervised 134/200), control rows

hypothesis: A pe=none looped encoder trained at 8-16 keeps its candidate ranking at sizes it never saw.
notes: Sources: nn_labeler/results/audit_prod_v1_s11_full.json, audit_coarse_g40r4/g48r4.json, self_play_robots/results/audit/labeler_prod_v1_s11_g56g64.json (job 4707188). Documented in supervised_valuenet FINDINGS (labeler track) and self_play_robots FINDINGS 17.
variant_conclusion: It worked: on boards up to 64x64 - four times its training size - it picks a truly best candidate 81-92% of the time, and it seeded nearly every later network in the project.
variant_description: A network that estimates how many steps a plan still needs, used to label training data instead of a slow exact solver. Its trick: nothing in it is tied to a specific board size, so one network trained only on small boards (8-16) can label boards of any size. Technically: LoopedValueNet, no positional encoding, trained on exact labels at 8x8-16x16.
